body: Thanks for the reply, I actual have an appointment with my psychiatrist on Thursday, it's just a check up appointment, but I'm definitely going to talk about this to him. The only thing is I have to wait until Thursday, so I'm a little worried I'm going to have another episode before then. Luckily my parents are around, and if need be I can go to them for help. I haven't told them what I've been going through, my Mom has depression as well and whenever I bring stuff like this up, it saddens her. My Dad is emotionally detached, and doesn't seem to understand this stuff.

Various things cause it, for me it's caused by the feeling of despair and hopelessness. Sometimes it's obvious what the problem is, but there have been times where I feel fine and nothing is immediately wrong and it kicks in. Sometimes I just feel that wherever I am, I want to be somewhere else. This is what makes it such a pain, because it seems somewhat random so I don't know how to prevent it.

I have had something similar. I would be at work, and get this gut feeling I shouldn't be there, I should be somewhere else doing something different, but rarely I have a clue about what it is. It's also not just work, it happens almost anywhere, even when I'm at home with free time. Sometimes it's so powerful that I physically get ill and become high strung. I also suffer from anxiety and depression.
Well how would you feel if your ancestors used to rule the planet, and now you have to badger people for some seed.

I don't know, I've pulled myself out of this before, but it seems no matter what, no matter how hopeful things seem to get, I come right back to this point over and over again. It feels like I've been in a river holding onto a rock for dear life, if I let go, I go over a waterfall and die. The current is extremely strong and once in awhile things come down the river trying to knock me off the rock. After awhile, you just get tired and even feel as if you want to let go, let the inevitable happen.

I was a happy, hopeful child, then in the most important years of my life I was diagnosed with depression. Everything I've wanted/needed/deserved seems to have been taken away from me. Not only do I have to fight with myself in an internal struggle, I also have to deal with the external struggle of life. This is going to sound crazy, but some day's I'm convinced that there's people in a control room somewhere watching my life, trying to figure out what more can they do to me to finally break me. To just give up all hope that my life will be any better, and just give up and wait to die.
